source_text: Sed ut de definitione iustitiae, ita etiam de peccati conditione dissertum est, quod peccatum apparuit nihil esse aliud quam malam voluntatem, cui esset liberum ab eo, quod prave appetiverat, abstinere.
pass_a_gloss: But as about the definition of justice, so also it has been discussed about the condition of sin, that sin has appeared to be nothing other than an evil will, to which it was free to abstain from that which it had crookedly desired.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS liber=free; Blaise unde liberum est abstinere
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: Just as we discussed the definition of justice, we also discussed the nature of sin. Sin proved to be nothing other than an evil will that was free to refrain from what it wrongly desired.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
